'''''Hesperocyparis glabra''''', known as the '''Arizona smooth bark cypress''' or '''smooth Arizona cypress''', is a [[conifer]] in the cypress family, [[Cupressaceae]], native to the American Southwest, with a range stretching over the canyons and slopes in a somewhat wide vicinity around [[Sedona, Arizona]]. It is distinguished from ''[[Hesperocyparis arizonica]]'' by its very smooth, non-furrowed bark which can appear in shades of pink, cherry, and grey.<ref name="Gymnosperm DB">{{cite web |last1=Earle |first1=Christopher J. |title=Hesperocyparis glabra (smooth Arizona cypress) description |url=https://www.conifers.org/cu/Hesperocyparis_glabra.php |website=The Gymnosperm Database |access-date=14 February 2024 |date=2023}}</ref>

It is often seen in cultivation, as unlike the [[Cupressus macrocarpa|Monterey cypress]], it has proved to be very resistant to [[cypress canker]].<ref name="NC Extension">{{cite web |title=Hesperocyparis glabra (Arizona Cypress, Cuyamaca Cypress, Piute Cypress, Smooth Arizona Cypress) |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/hesperocyparis-glabra/ |website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |publisher=North Carolina State University |access-date=15 February 2024}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Hesperocyparis glabra'' was scientifically described by [[George Bishop Sudworth]] in 1910 with the name of ''Cupressus glabra''.<ref name="POWO" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sudworth |first1=George Bishop |author1-link=George Bishop Sudworth |title=A New Cypress for Arizona |journal=American Forestry |date=1910 |volume=16 |pages=88-90 |url=https://archive.org/details/americanforestry161910amer/page/88 |access-date=14 February 2024 |publisher=American Forestry Association |location=Washington, D.C. |language=en}}</ref> In 1966 the botanist [[Elbert Luther Little]] published a paper where he argued that it was a subspecies of what was then ''Cupressus arizonica''.<ref name="POWO" /> Along with the other new world ''[[Cupressus]]'' species it was transferred to the new genus ''[[Hesperocyparis]]'' in 2009. At the same time the authors restored it as a species under its present name.<ref name="POWO" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Adams |first1=Robert P. |last2=Bartel |first2=Jim A. |last3=Price |first3=Robert A. |title=A new genus, ''Hesperocyparis'', for the cypresses of the Western Hemisphere |journal=[[Phytologia]] |date=2009 |volume=91 |issue=1 |pages=160–185 |url=http://www.phytologia.org/uploads/2/3/4/2/23422706/911160-185adamsbartelhesperocyparis.pdf |access-date=14 February 2024}}</ref>

{{As of|2024}} ''Hesperocyparis glabra'' is listed as the accepted species name with no subspecies by [[Plants of the World Online]] (POWO),<ref name="POWO" /> [[World Flora Online]],<ref>{{Cite WFO |title=''Hesperocyparis glabra'' (Sudw.) Bartel |id=0000912966 |access-date=14 February 2024}}</ref> and the USDA [[Natural Resources Conservation Service]] PLANTS database (PLANTS).<ref name="USDA">{{cite usda plants|symbol=HEGL4 |title=Hesperocyparis glabra |date=14 February 2024}}</ref>
